items.stem: What happens to the demand curve for a normal good when consumers' incomes rise?
options: There is a movement along it
items.answer: It shifts to the right
items.markingKey: A. More is demanded at every price.

items.stem: Briefly explain why an advertising campaign shifts the demand curve rather than causing a movement along it.
items.answer: Advertising changes consumer tastes, a non-price factor, so more is demanded at every price; a movement along the curve happens only when the good's own price changes.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Advertising changes consumer tastes, a non-price factor, so more is demanded at every price; a movement along the curve happens only when the good's own price changes. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: A student claims: "If incomes rise, demand for every good rises." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Demand for inferior goods, such as some cheap staple foods or bus travel, may fall as people switch to better alternatives.
items.markingKey: Demand for inferior goods, such as some cheap staple foods or bus travel, may fall as people switch to better alternatives. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Which of the following is the most clear and focused research question for an investigation into demand and supply and the factors that determine them?
options: How did the price of cocoa change between 2022 and 2024, and what supply factors explain the change?
items.answer: How did the price of cocoa change between 2022 and 2024, and what supply factors explain the change?
items.markingKey: B. It is open, has a clear scope (place/period/group) and can be answered with evidence; the others are too broad, closed or off-topic.

items.stem: Write one well-structured paragraph (Point, Evidence, Explanation, Link) in answer to this question: Explain why supply curves usually slope upwards.
items.answer: Higher prices make production more profitable, so existing firms produce more and new firms are attracted into the market.
items.markingKey: Content: Higher prices make production more profitable, so existing firms produce more and new firms are attracted into the market. Structure: a clear point that answers the question, specific evidence, explanation that links evidence to the point, and a closing link. Criterion C (communicating): appropriate style and register for the purpose, a clear structure suited to the format (topic sentence, developed evidence, explanation, link back to the question), accurate subject terminology, and sources documented with a recognised convention (MLA or APA).

items.stem:
Source A – Market report (paraphrased): Paraphrase of reports by the International Cocoa Organization and financial news, 2024

The report stated that cocoa prices had more than tripled in a year because poor weather and plant disease in Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana, which grow over half the world's cocoa, had reduced harvests. Chocolate makers said they would raise prices or reduce bar sizes.

What is the message of Source A about demand and supply and the factors that determine them? Refer to details in the source.
items.answer: Bad weather and disease reduced the cocoa supply, raising prices sharply.
items.markingKey: Bad weather and disease reduced the cocoa supply, raising prices sharply. Award 1 mark per relevant point drawn from the source, up to [3]; own knowledge is not credited here. Criterion D: interpreting a source.

items.stem:
Source A – Market report (paraphrased): Paraphrase of reports by the International Cocoa Organization and financial news, 2024

The report stated that cocoa prices had more than tripled in a year because poor weather and plant disease in Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana, which grow over half the world's cocoa, had reduced harvests. Chocolate makers said they would raise prices or reduce bar sizes.

With reference to its origin and purpose, analyse the value and limitations of Source A for a student investigating demand and supply and the factors that determine them.
items.answer: Origin: Paraphrase of reports by the International Cocoa Organization and financial news, 2024. Purpose: to inform traders, businesses and the public about market conditions. Value: It explains a real supply shock with expert data on production. Limitation: It focuses on producers and businesses and says little about the effect on cocoa farmers' incomes.
items.markingKey: Origin: Paraphrase of reports by the International Cocoa Organization and financial news, 2024. Purpose: to inform traders, businesses and the public about market conditions. Value: It explains a real supply shock with expert data on production. Limitation: It focuses on producers and businesses and says little about the effect on cocoa farmers' incomes. Award up to [3]: origin and purpose identified and USED (not just copied), at least one value and one limitation explicitly linked to them. Reliability is judged for a purpose, not as "biased = useless". MYP I&S criterion D (year 4), scaled to the marks: 7-8 discusses concepts, issues and theories in detail, synthesises information to make valid, well-supported arguments, analyses and evaluates a range of sources in terms of origin and purpose, examining value and limitations, and interprets different perspectives and their implications; 5-6 substantial; 3-4 adequate, partly descriptive; 1-2 limited, mostly assertion.

items.stem: "Consumer income is the most important factor determining demand." Discuss.
items.answer: Income is a key factor, but its importance depends on the good; for fashion goods tastes may dominate and for necessities price and population matter more.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: income sets what people are able to buy; rising incomes in Asia transformed demand for cars and meat. Arguments against: tastes, the price of substitutes and population size also matter; for necessities, demand changes little with income. Supported judgement: Income is a key factor, but its importance depends on the good; for fashion goods tastes may dominate and for necessities price and population matter more. Markbands (8 marks): MYP I&S criterion D (year 4), scaled to the marks: 7-8 discusses concepts, issues and theories in detail, synthesises information to make valid, well-supported arguments, analyses and evaluates a range of sources in terms of origin and purpose, examining value and limitations, and interprets different perspectives and their implications; 5-6 substantial; 3-4 adequate, partly descriptive; 1-2 limited, mostly assertion.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "substitute"?
options: A good that is used together with another, such as printers and ink cartridges
The price at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied, so the market clears
A good that can be used in place of another, such as tea and coffee
When quantity demanded is greater than quantity supplied at the current price
items.answer: A good that can be used in place of another, such as tea and coffee
items.markingKey: C. "substitute" is a good that can be used in place of another, such as tea and coffee.

items.stem: Briefly explain why new technology usually shifts supply to the right.
items.answer: Technology lowers the cost of producing each unit, so firms can supply more at every price.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Technology lowers the cost of producing each unit, so firms can supply more at every price. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Distinguish between a complementary good and a substitute good.
items.answer: A rise in the price of a substitute increases demand for the other good; a rise in the price of a complement reduces demand for the other good.
items.markingKey: A rise in the price of a substitute increases demand for the other good; a rise in the price of a complement reduces demand for the other good. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Explain why "How did the price of cocoa change between 2022 and 2024, and what supply factors explain the change?" is a suitable research question for an MYP investigation into demand and supply and the factors that determine them.
items.answer: It links demand and supply theory to a real commodity market.
items.markingKey: It links demand and supply theory to a real commodity market. Award marks for relevance to the unit's concepts or global context, and for showing the question is focused and can be answered with available sources. Criterion B (investigating): a clear, focused research question whose relevance is justified, a realistic action plan, appropriate and varied methods/sources, and reflection on the process.

items.stem: A class brainstorm on demand and supply and the factors that determine them produced the question "Why are things expensive?" Explain why it needs refining, then suggest an improved research question and justify your change.
items.answer: Weakness: it is far too broad and has no focus Improved: "How did the price of cocoa change between 2022 and 2024, and what supply factors explain the change?"
items.markingKey: 1 mark: weakness identified (it is far too broad and has no focus); 1-2 marks: a focused question such as "How did the price of cocoa change between 2022 and 2024, and what supply factors explain the change?" (clear scope – place, period or group – and open, researchable wording); 1 mark: justification of the change. Criterion B (investigating): a clear, focused research question whose relevance is justified, a realistic action plan, appropriate and varied methods/sources, and reflection on the process.

items.stem: You have three weeks to investigate "How did the price of cocoa change between 2022 and 2024, and what supply factors explain the change?" Outline a step-by-step plan, the sources you would use and one way you would evaluate your process at the end.
items.answer: Collect ICCO price data; read reports on weather and disease in West Africa; draw supply-and-demand diagrams; compare factors; evaluate sources; cite in APA.
items.markingKey: Indicative plan: Collect ICCO price data; read reports on weather and disease in West Africa; draw supply-and-demand diagrams; compare factors; evaluate sources; cite in APA. Credit: logical sequence of steps with a timeline; varied, appropriate sources (primary and secondary) named specifically; a method for recording and citing information (e.g. a source log in MLA/APA); a step for evaluating the process and results. Criterion B (investigating): a clear, focused research question whose relevance is justified, a realistic action plan, appropriate and varied methods/sources, and reflection on the process.

items.stem: Plan an extended response to the question: "Consumer income is the most important factor determining demand." To what extent do you agree? Give a thesis, two arguments with specific evidence, a counter-argument and a conclusion.
items.answer: Thesis: Income is a key factor, but its importance depends on the good; for fashion goods tastes may dominate and for necessities price and population matter more.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: income sets what people are able to buy; rising incomes in Asia transformed demand for cars and meat. Counter-arguments: tastes, the price of substitutes and population size also matter; for necessities, demand changes little with income. Thesis/conclusion: Income is a key factor, but its importance depends on the good; for fashion goods tastes may dominate and for necessities price and population matter more. Credit a thesis that answers the question, logically ordered paragraphs each with specific evidence, a counter-argument that is weighed, and a conclusion that follows. Criterion C (communicating): appropriate style and register for the purpose, a clear structure suited to the format (topic sentence, developed evidence, explanation, link back to the question), accurate subject terminology, and sources documented with a recognised convention (MLA or APA).

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "market"?
options: The way changes in prices signal and ration resources, bringing markets towards equilibrium
Any arrangement that allows buyers and sellers to exchange goods, services or resources
In India, a price at which the government buys crops such as wheat and rice from farmers
When quantity supplied is greater than quantity demanded at the current price
items.answer: Any arrangement that allows buyers and sellers to exchange goods, services or resources
items.markingKey: B. "market" is any arrangement that allows buyers and sellers to exchange goods, services or resources.

items.stem: "Once a market reaches equilibrium it stays there forever." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Equilibrium changes whenever demand or supply shift, for example after a harvest failure or a change in tastes.
items.markingKey: Equilibrium changes whenever demand or supply shift, for example after a harvest failure or a change in tastes. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Distinguish between a shortage and a surplus.
items.answer: A shortage occurs when price is below equilibrium and demand exceeds supply; a surplus occurs when price is above equilibrium and supply exceeds demand.
items.markingKey: A shortage occurs when price is below equilibrium and demand exceeds supply; a surplus occurs when price is above equilibrium and supply exceeds demand. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: In the market for umbrellas in Singapore, demand and supply are given by Qd = 165 − 3P and Qs = 2P + 140 (P in S$, Q in umbrellas per day). Calculate the equilibrium price and quantity.
items.answer: P = 5 S$, Q = 150 umbrellas

items.stem: Evaluate the research question "What is a market?" for an MYP Individuals and Societies investigation into price determination: equilibrium, shortages and surpluses. Rewrite it so that it is clear, focused and researchable.
items.answer: Weakness: it is a definition question Improved: "How did shortages of semiconductors affect new car prices in the United States between 2020 and 2022?"
items.markingKey: 1 mark: weakness identified (it is a definition question); 1-2 marks: a focused question such as "How did shortages of semiconductors affect new car prices in the United States between 2020 and 2022?" (clear scope – place, period or group – and open, researchable wording); 1 mark: justification of the change. Criterion B (investigating): a clear, focused research question whose relevance is justified, a realistic action plan, appropriate and varied methods/sources, and reflection on the process.

items.stem:
Source A – Economics text (paraphrased): Paraphrase of Adam Smith, An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations, London, 1776

The author argued that individuals pursuing their own interest are often led, as if by an invisible hand, to promote the interests of society more effectively than if they intended to do so. A butcher or baker, he wrote, provides our dinner not out of kindness but out of regard for their own interest.

Outline the main argument or view that Source A presents, quoting or referring to the source.
items.answer: Self-interest in markets can benefit society through the invisible hand.
items.markingKey: Self-interest in markets can benefit society through the invisible hand. Award 1 mark per relevant point drawn from the source, up to [3]; own knowledge is not credited here. Criterion D: interpreting a source.

items.stem: Describe the research methods you would use to answer "How did shortages of semiconductors affect new car prices in the United States between 2020 and 2022?", naming specific sources and explaining why each is appropriate.
items.answer: Collect price data (US Bureau of Labor Statistics); read two industry reports; draw demand and supply diagrams; consider other factors; evaluate sources; cite in APA.
items.markingKey: Indicative plan: Collect price data (US Bureau of Labor Statistics); read two industry reports; draw demand and supply diagrams; consider other factors; evaluate sources; cite in APA. Credit: logical sequence of steps with a timeline; varied, appropriate sources (primary and secondary) named specifically; a method for recording and citing information (e.g. a source log in MLA/APA); a step for evaluating the process and results. Criterion B (investigating): a clear, focused research question whose relevance is justified, a realistic action plan, appropriate and varied methods/sources, and reflection on the process.

items.stem: Evaluate the claim: "The price mechanism is the best way to allocate scarce resources."
items.answer: The price mechanism is efficient for most goods, but governments may need to intervene for necessities and when markets fail.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: prices signal scarcity and encourage efficient production; markets respond quickly without central planning. Arguments against: people on low incomes may be unable to afford necessities; markets may fail to account for external costs such as pollution. Supported judgement: The price mechanism is efficient for most goods, but governments may need to intervene for necessities and when markets fail. Markbands (8 marks): MYP I&S criterion D (year 4), scaled to the marks: 7-8 discusses concepts, issues and theories in detail, synthesises information to make valid, well-supported arguments, analyses and evaluates a range of sources in terms of origin and purpose, examining value and limitations, and interprets different perspectives and their implications; 5-6 substantial; 3-4 adequate, partly descriptive; 1-2 limited, mostly assertion.

items.stem: Define the term "equilibrium quantity".
items.answer: The quantity bought and sold at the equilibrium price
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: the quantity bought and sold at the equilibrium price. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Explain why concert tickets are often resold above face value.
items.answer: Tickets are priced below equilibrium, creating excess demand; resellers buy them and sell at the higher price fans are willing to pay.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Tickets are priced below equilibrium, creating excess demand; resellers buy them and sell at the higher price fans are willing to pay. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Distinguish between the equilibrium price and the market price.
items.answer: The equilibrium price is where demand equals supply; the market price is the price actually charged at a given moment, which may be above or below equilibrium.
items.markingKey: The equilibrium price is where demand equals supply; the market price is the price actually charged at a given moment, which may be above or below equilibrium. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem:
Source A – Economics text (paraphrased): Paraphrase of Adam Smith, An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations, London, 1776

The author argued that individuals pursuing their own interest are often led, as if by an invisible hand, to promote the interests of society more effectively than if they intended to do so. A butcher or baker, he wrote, provides our dinner not out of kindness but out of regard for their own interest.

How reliable is Source A for someone researching price determination: equilibrium, shortages and surpluses? Justify your answer using its origin and purpose.
items.answer: Origin: Paraphrase of Adam Smith, An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations, London, 1776. Purpose: to argue for free markets against heavy government regulation of trade. Value: It is a founding text of economics and shows how prices coordinate decisions. Limitation: It was written in the 18th century before large corporations and modern environmental problems; Smith also warned about monopolies.
items.markingKey: Origin: Paraphrase of Adam Smith, An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations, London, 1776. Purpose: to argue for free markets against heavy government regulation of trade. Value: It is a founding text of economics and shows how prices coordinate decisions. Limitation: It was written in the 18th century before large corporations and modern environmental problems; Smith also warned about monopolies. Award up to [3]: origin and purpose identified and USED (not just copied), at least one value and one limitation explicitly linked to them. Reliability is judged for a purpose, not as "biased = useless". MYP I&S criterion D (year 4), scaled to the marks: 7-8 discusses concepts, issues and theories in detail, synthesises information to make valid, well-supported arguments, analyses and evaluates a range of sources in terms of origin and purpose, examining value and limitations, and interprets different perspectives and their implications; 5-6 substantial; 3-4 adequate, partly descriptive; 1-2 limited, mostly assertion.

items.stem: For bicycles in Amsterdam, Qd = 200 − 5P and Qs = 20 + 4P. What exists at a price of 18?
items.answer: A shortage of 18 units
items.markingKey: D. Qd = 110, Qs = 92; equilibrium price is 20.

"The price mechanism is the best way to allocate scarce resources." Using Source A and your own knowledge, to what extent do you agree?

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "rationing"?
options: A legal lower limit on price, set above equilibrium to help producers or workers, such as a minimum wage
Distributing a limited supply of goods by quotas, queues or coupons rather than by price
When quantity demanded is greater than quantity supplied at the current price
The way changes in prices signal and ration resources, bringing markets towards equilibrium
items.answer: Distributing a limited supply of goods by quotas, queues or coupons rather than by price
items.markingKey: B. "rationing" is distributing a limited supply of goods by quotas, queues or coupons rather than by price.

items.stem: Briefly explain why a subsidy on solar panels can increase their use.
items.answer: The subsidy lowers producers' costs, shifting supply right, so the price falls and more households and businesses buy solar panels.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: The subsidy lowers producers' costs, shifting supply right, so the price falls and more households and businesses buy solar panels. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Tomás writes: "The producer pays all of an indirect tax." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: The tax burden is shared; consumers usually pay part through higher prices, depending on how responsive demand is.
items.markingKey: The tax burden is shared; consumers usually pay part through higher prices, depending on how responsive demand is. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem:
Source A – Government evaluation (paraphrased): Paraphrase of Public Health England, Sugar reduction: report on progress, 2020

The report found that the soft drinks levy, introduced in April 2018, had led manufacturers to reduce the sugar content of many drinks before the levy started. The total sugar sold in soft drinks fell by about a third between 2015 and 2019, while sales volumes of soft drinks increased.

Outline the main argument or view that Source A presents, quoting or referring to the source.
items.answer: The levy led firms to cut sugar, and sugar sold in drinks fell.
items.markingKey: The levy led firms to cut sugar, and sugar sold in drinks fell. Award 1 mark per relevant point drawn from the source, up to [2]; own knowledge is not credited here. Criterion D: interpreting a source.

items.stem: For ferry tickets in Istanbul: Qd = 334 − 2P and Qs = 3P + 249 (P in lira). The government introduces a subsidy of 4 lira per unit to producers. Calculate the new equilibrium price paid by consumers and the new quantity, and explain why governments might do this.
items.answer: Consumer price 14.60 lira; quantity 304.8 tickets
items.markingKey: Original equilibrium P = 17, Q = 300 (A1). New supply Qs = 3(P + 4) + 249 (M1); solve: P = 14.60 (A1), Q = 304.8 (A1). Government spending = 4 × 304.8 = 1219.2 (A1). Reason (R1): to make a merit good or green technology cheaper and encourage consumption. Price changes by less than 4 because the burden/benefit is shared.

items.stem: You have three weeks to investigate "To what extent did the UK soft drinks industry levy reduce sugar consumption between 2016 and 2022?" Outline a step-by-step plan, the sources you would use and one way you would evaluate your process at the end.
items.answer: Use Public Health England data and two academic studies; compare sugar per 100 ml before and after; consider other influences; evaluate sources; cite in APA.
items.markingKey: Indicative plan: Use Public Health England data and two academic studies; compare sugar per 100 ml before and after; consider other influences; evaluate sources; cite in APA. Credit: logical sequence of steps with a timeline; varied, appropriate sources (primary and secondary) named specifically; a method for recording and citing information (e.g. a source log in MLA/APA); a step for evaluating the process and results. Criterion B (investigating): a clear, focused research question whose relevance is justified, a realistic action plan, appropriate and varied methods/sources, and reflection on the process.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "A legal upper limit on the price of a good, set below equilibrium to help consumers"?
items.answer: maximum price (price ceiling)
items.markingKey: B. This is the definition of maximum price (price ceiling).

items.stem: Explain the difference between a maximum price and a minimum price.
items.answer: A maximum price is set below equilibrium to protect consumers and tends to cause shortages; a minimum price is set above equilibrium to protect producers and tends to cause surpluses.
items.markingKey: A maximum price is set below equilibrium to protect consumers and tends to cause shortages; a minimum price is set above equilibrium to protect producers and tends to cause surpluses. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Ana writes: "Subsidies are free for society." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Subsidies are paid from taxes or borrowing, so they have an opportunity cost.
items.markingKey: Subsidies are paid from taxes or borrowing, so they have an opportunity cost. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Which of the following is the most clear and focused research question for an investigation into government intervention in markets through price controls, taxes and subsidies?
options: To what extent did the UK soft drinks industry levy reduce sugar consumption between 2016 and 2022?
items.answer: To what extent did the UK soft drinks industry levy reduce sugar consumption between 2016 and 2022?
items.markingKey: C. It is open, has a clear scope (place/period/group) and can be answered with evidence; the others are too broad, closed or off-topic.

items.stem: Plan an extended response to the question: "Taxes on sugary drinks are an effective way to reduce obesity." To what extent do you agree? Give a thesis, two arguments with specific evidence, a counter-argument and a conclusion.
items.answer: Thesis: Sugar taxes help reduce sugar intake, especially through reformulation, but they work best as part of a wider strategy including education and regulation.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: taxes raise prices and in the UK led firms to cut sugar content; revenue can fund school sport and health programmes. Counter-arguments: consumers may switch to other unhealthy foods; the tax falls more heavily on low-income households. Thesis/conclusion: Sugar taxes help reduce sugar intake, especially through reformulation, but they work best as part of a wider strategy including education and regulation. Credit a thesis that answers the question, logically ordered paragraphs each with specific evidence, a counter-argument that is weighed, and a conclusion that follows. Criterion C (communicating): appropriate style and register for the purpose, a clear structure suited to the format (topic sentence, developed evidence, explanation, link back to the question), accurate subject terminology, and sources documented with a recognised convention (MLA or APA).

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "The quantity of a good or service that producers are willing and able to sell at each price over a period of time"?
items.answer: supply
items.markingKey: C. This is the definition of supply.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "The price at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied, so the market clears"?
items.answer: equilibrium price
items.markingKey: C. This is the definition of equilibrium price.

items.stem: How does a subsidy affect the supply curve?
options: It shifts supply to the right
It shifts demand to the left
It shifts supply to the left
items.answer: It shifts supply to the right
items.markingKey: A. Producers' costs fall.

items.stem: Distinguish between a movement along the demand curve and a shift of the demand curve.
items.answer: A movement is caused by a change in the good's own price; a shift is caused by a change in a non-price factor such as income, tastes or the price of related goods.
items.markingKey: A movement is caused by a change in the good's own price; a shift is caused by a change in a non-price factor such as income, tastes or the price of related goods. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Explain how the price mechanism rations scarce goods.
items.answer: When a good is scarce, its price rises, so only those willing and able to pay buy it, while the higher price encourages producers to supply more.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: When a good is scarce, its price rises, so only those willing and able to pay buy it, while the higher price encourages producers to supply more. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain the difference between an indirect tax and a subsidy.
items.answer: An indirect tax raises costs and shifts supply left, raising price; a subsidy lowers costs and shifts supply right, lowering price.
items.markingKey: An indirect tax raises costs and shifts supply left, raising price; a subsidy lowers costs and shifts supply right, lowering price. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Mohammed writes: "Supply means the amount of a good that exists." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Supply is the amount producers are willing and able to sell at each price over a period, not the total stock.
items.markingKey: Supply is the amount producers are willing and able to sell at each price over a period, not the total stock. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: A student claims: "A shortage means there are no goods at all." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: A shortage means quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied at the current price; some goods are still sold.
items.markingKey: A shortage means quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied at the current price; some goods are still sold. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Distinguish between a minimum price and a maximum price.
items.answer: A maximum price is set below equilibrium to protect consumers and tends to cause shortages; a minimum price is set above equilibrium to protect producers and tends to cause surpluses.
items.markingKey: A maximum price is set below equilibrium to protect consumers and tends to cause shortages; a minimum price is set above equilibrium to protect producers and tends to cause surpluses. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

Judgement (1-2 marks): Sugar taxes help reduce sugar intake, especially through reformulation, but they work best as part of a wider strategy including education and regulation.

items.stem: In the market for umbrellas in Singapore, demand and supply are given by Qd = 244 − 3P and Qs = 4P + 118 (P in S$, Q in umbrellas per day). Calculate the equilibrium price and quantity.
items.answer: P = 18 S$, Q = 190 umbrellas

items.stem: Write one well-structured paragraph (Point, Evidence, Explanation, Link) in answer to this question: Explain why a surplus causes the price to fall.
items.answer: Sellers have unsold stock, so they cut prices to attract buyers; as price falls quantity demanded rises and quantity supplied falls until the surplus disappears.
items.markingKey: Content: Sellers have unsold stock, so they cut prices to attract buyers; as price falls quantity demanded rises and quantity supplied falls until the surplus disappears. Structure: a clear point that answers the question, specific evidence, explanation that links evidence to the point, and a closing link. Criterion C (communicating): appropriate style and register for the purpose, a clear structure suited to the format (topic sentence, developed evidence, explanation, link back to the question), accurate subject terminology, and sources documented with a recognised convention (MLA or APA).

items.stem: Using accurate subject terminology and at least one specific example, write a structured paragraph that responds to: Explain why governments tax goods such as cigarettes.
items.answer: The tax raises the price, reducing consumption of a harmful good, and raises revenue that can fund healthcare.
items.markingKey: Content: The tax raises the price, reducing consumption of a harmful good, and raises revenue that can fund healthcare. Structure: a clear point that answers the question, specific evidence, explanation that links evidence to the point, and a closing link. Criterion C (communicating): appropriate style and register for the purpose, a clear structure suited to the format (topic sentence, developed evidence, explanation, link back to the question), accurate subject terminology, and sources documented with a recognised convention (MLA or APA).

items.stem: Freya argues that "Consumer income is the most important factor determining demand." Kwame disagrees. Explain one piece of evidence each student could use, and state which view you find more convincing and why.
items.answer: Income is a key factor, but its importance depends on the good; for fashion goods tastes may dominate and for necessities price and population matter more.
items.markingKey: Freya: income sets what people are able to buy. Kwame: tastes, the price of substitutes and population size also matter. Judgement (1-2 marks): Income is a key factor, but its importance depends on the good; for fashion goods tastes may dominate and for necessities price and population matter more.

items.stem: Write the introduction and an outline of the body paragraphs for an essay that evaluates the view that "The price mechanism is the best way to allocate scarce resources."
items.answer: Thesis: The price mechanism is efficient for most goods, but governments may need to intervene for necessities and when markets fail.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: prices signal scarcity and encourage efficient production; markets respond quickly without central planning. Counter-arguments: people on low incomes may be unable to afford necessities; markets may fail to account for external costs such as pollution. Thesis/conclusion: The price mechanism is efficient for most goods, but governments may need to intervene for necessities and when markets fail. Credit a thesis that answers the question, logically ordered paragraphs each with specific evidence, a counter-argument that is weighed, and a conclusion that follows. Criterion C (communicating): appropriate style and register for the purpose, a clear structure suited to the format (topic sentence, developed evidence, explanation, link back to the question), accurate subject terminology, and sources documented with a recognised convention (MLA or APA).

items.stem: Evaluate the research question "Are taxes good?" for an MYP Individuals and Societies investigation into government intervention in markets through price controls, taxes and subsidies. Rewrite it so that it is clear, focused and researchable.
items.answer: Weakness: it is a vague value question Improved: "To what extent did the UK soft drinks industry levy reduce sugar consumption between 2016 and 2022?"
items.markingKey: 1 mark: weakness identified (it is a vague value question); 1-2 marks: a focused question such as "To what extent did the UK soft drinks industry levy reduce sugar consumption between 2016 and 2022?" (clear scope – place, period or group – and open, researchable wording); 1 mark: justification of the change. Criterion B (investigating): a clear, focused research question whose relevance is justified, a realistic action plan, appropriate and varied methods/sources, and reflection on the process.

items.stem:
Source A – Market report (paraphrased): Paraphrase of reports by the International Cocoa Organization and financial news, 2024

The report stated that cocoa prices had more than tripled in a year because poor weather and plant disease in Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana, which grow over half the world's cocoa, had reduced harvests. Chocolate makers said they would raise prices or reduce bar sizes.

Using Source A and your own knowledge, evaluate the claim that "Consumer income is the most important factor determining demand."
items.answer: Income is a key factor, but its importance depends on the good; for fashion goods tastes may dominate and for necessities price and population matter more.
items.markingKey: From the source: Bad weather and disease reduced the cocoa supply, raising prices sharply. Own knowledge for: income sets what people are able to buy; rising incomes in Asia transformed demand for cars and meat. Own knowledge against: tastes, the price of substitutes and population size also matter; for necessities, demand changes little with income. Judgement: Income is a key factor, but its importance depends on the good; for fashion goods tastes may dominate and for necessities price and population matter more. Top answers integrate the source with own knowledge and comment on the source's origin/purpose. MYP I&S criterion D (year 4), scaled to the marks: 7-8 discusses concepts, issues and theories in detail, synthesises information to make valid, well-supported arguments, analyses and evaluates a range of sources in terms of origin and purpose, examining value and limitations, and interprets different perspectives and their implications; 5-6 substantial; 3-4 adequate, partly descriptive; 1-2 limited, mostly assertion.

items.stem: You have three weeks to investigate "How did shortages of semiconductors affect new car prices in the United States between 2020 and 2022?" Outline a step-by-step plan, the sources you would use and one way you would evaluate your process at the end.
items.answer: Collect price data (US Bureau of Labor Statistics); read two industry reports; draw demand and supply diagrams; consider other factors; evaluate sources; cite in APA.
items.markingKey: Indicative plan: Collect price data (US Bureau of Labor Statistics); read two industry reports; draw demand and supply diagrams; consider other factors; evaluate sources; cite in APA. Credit: logical sequence of steps with a timeline; varied, appropriate sources (primary and secondary) named specifically; a method for recording and citing information (e.g. a source log in MLA/APA); a step for evaluating the process and results. Criterion B (investigating): a clear, focused research question whose relevance is justified, a realistic action plan, appropriate and varied methods/sources, and reflection on the process.

items.stem: Define the term "substitute".
items.answer: A good that can be used in place of another, such as tea and coffee
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: a good that can be used in place of another, such as tea and coffee. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: At a price above the equilibrium, what exists in the market?
items.answer: A surplus (excess supply)
items.markingKey: C. Producers want to sell more than consumers want to buy.

items.stem: A national minimum wage is an example of what?
items.answer: A minimum price in the labour market
items.markingKey: A minimum price in the labour market. It sets a floor on the price of labour.

items.stem: Sana writes: "An increase in price causes demand to fall." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: A price rise causes a fall in quantity demanded (a movement along the curve); demand itself (the curve) shifts only when non-price factors change.
items.markingKey: A price rise causes a fall in quantity demanded (a movement along the curve); demand itself (the curve) shifts only when non-price factors change. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: A student claims: "Once a market reaches equilibrium it stays there forever." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Equilibrium changes whenever demand or supply shift, for example after a harvest failure or a change in tastes.
items.markingKey: Equilibrium changes whenever demand or supply shift, for example after a harvest failure or a change in tastes. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Briefly explain why a minimum price for crops can create a surplus.
items.answer: At a guaranteed price above equilibrium, farmers produce more while consumers buy less, so the government must buy and store the excess, as happened with grain stocks in India.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: At a guaranteed price above equilibrium, farmers produce more while consumers buy less, so the government must buy and store the excess, as happened with grain stocks in India. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain the difference between a complementary good and a substitute good.
items.answer: A rise in the price of a substitute increases demand for the other good; a rise in the price of a complement reduces demand for the other good.
items.markingKey: A rise in the price of a substitute increases demand for the other good; a rise in the price of a complement reduces demand for the other good. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Explain the difference between the equilibrium price and the market price.
items.answer: The equilibrium price is where demand equals supply; the market price is the price actually charged at a given moment, which may be above or below equilibrium.
items.markingKey: The equilibrium price is where demand equals supply; the market price is the price actually charged at a given moment, which may be above or below equilibrium. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: A student claims: "Price controls always help the people they are meant to help." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: They can backfire: rent controls may reduce housing supply and some tenants cannot find homes; minimum prices can create waste.
items.markingKey: They can backfire: rent controls may reduce housing supply and some tenants cannot find homes; minimum prices can create waste. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

(a) Identify the equilibrium price. (b) State whether there is a shortage or surplus at 9 €, and how large it is.
items.answer: (a) 6 € (110 bicycles); (b) surplus of 165 bicycles
items.markingKey: (a) Equilibrium where demand = supply: 6 €, 110 bicycles (A1). (b) At 9: supply 170 > demand 5 → surplus (R1) of 165 (A1).

items.answer: The price mechanism is efficient for most goods, but governments may need to intervene for necessities and when markets fail.

items.stem:
Source A – Government evaluation (paraphrased): Paraphrase of Public Health England, Sugar reduction: report on progress, 2020

The report found that the soft drinks levy, introduced in April 2018, had led manufacturers to reduce the sugar content of many drinks before the levy started. The total sugar sold in soft drinks fell by about a third between 2015 and 2019, while sales volumes of soft drinks increased.

How reliable is Source A for someone researching government intervention in markets through price controls, taxes and subsidies? Justify your answer using its origin and purpose.
items.answer: Origin: Paraphrase of Public Health England, Sugar reduction: report on progress, 2020. Purpose: to evaluate a government policy and inform future health policy. Value: It uses large-scale sales data and is produced by a public health agency. Limitation: As a government report it may emphasise success; it measures sugar sold rather than direct health outcomes.
items.markingKey: Origin: Paraphrase of Public Health England, Sugar reduction: report on progress, 2020. Purpose: to evaluate a government policy and inform future health policy. Value: It uses large-scale sales data and is produced by a public health agency. Limitation: As a government report it may emphasise success; it measures sugar sold rather than direct health outcomes. Award up to [3]: origin and purpose identified and USED (not just copied), at least one value and one limitation explicitly linked to them. Reliability is judged for a purpose, not as "biased = useless". MYP I&S criterion D (year 4), scaled to the marks: 7-8 discusses concepts, issues and theories in detail, synthesises information to make valid, well-supported arguments, analyses and evaluates a range of sources in terms of origin and purpose, examining value and limitations, and interprets different perspectives and their implications; 5-6 substantial; 3-4 adequate, partly descriptive; 1-2 limited, mostly assertion.

items.stem: According to approx., Eurostat, avocado imports into the European Union changed from 330 thousand tonnes (2012) to 760 thousand tonnes (2022). Calculate (a) the percentage change and (b) the average change in thousand tonnes per year.
items.answer: (a) +130.3%; (b) +43.00 thousand tonnes per year

items.stem: Briefly describe Venezuela's price controls and explain what it reveals about a maximum price creating a shortage.
items.answer: From 2003 the government set maximum prices for basic foods; by the mid-2010s shops faced severe shortages and long queues. Prices below equilibrium reduced supply and increased demand, leading to empty shelves.
items.markingKey: Context (From 2003 the government set maximum prices for basic foods; by the mid-2010s shops faced severe shortages and long queues.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: prices below equilibrium reduced supply and increased demand, leading to empty shelves. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to a maximum price creating a shortage.

items.stem: Using avocado demand in Europe and North America as an example, explain a change in tastes shifting demand.
items.answer: Health trends and social media made avocados fashionable in the 2010s; imports from Mexico and Peru grew rapidly. A non-price factor shifted demand to the right, raising prices and output.
items.markingKey: Context (Health trends and social media made avocados fashionable in the 2010s; imports from Mexico and Peru grew rapidly.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: a non-price factor shifted demand to the right, raising prices and output. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to a change in tastes shifting demand.

items.stem: In the market for phone cases in Kuala Lumpur, demand and supply are given by Qd = 360 − 4P and Qs = 4P + 280 (P in RM, Q in cases per day). Calculate the equilibrium price and quantity.
items.answer: P = 10 RM, Q = 320 cases
